solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: A cheerful setting for Byng's last ship

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the word for cheerful is placed around the chosen letter

parts.note: cheerful means rosy, as in a rosy outlook

indicators.note: last picks only the final letter of the admiral's name

explanation.surface: A jaunty memorial to Admiral Byng, executed in 1757, aboard his final vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting for' puts G, the last letter of Byng, inside ROSY, after the clue's A.
explanation.definitionFit: An argosy is a large merchant vessel of old, a poetic word for a richly laden ship.

clue.text: Relish cooked tripe and peas

indicators.note: cooked means messed with or rearranged, as in cooked books

explanation.surface: A tasty dish of cooked tripe and peas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the letters of TRIPE and PEAS; 'and' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is something that whets the appetite, as does a starter.

clue.text: Wind blowing hard around bachelor's part of building

indicators.note: around means the word for strong wind surrounds the letter

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
B is short for bachelor, as in degrees

explanation.surface: A howling wind batters the single man's section of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts B inside GALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gable is the triangular upper part of a wall at the end of a pitched roof.

clue.text: Act as Ulster tour guide, creating confrontation

parts.note: a tour guide shows visitors round; 'Act as' turns the guide into the verb
Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, in Ulster

explanation.surface: Escorting visitors around Northern Ireland leads to a stand-off.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNTY DOWN is in Ulster (Northern Ireland). To act as tour guide there is to show (people round) Down.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is a final decisive confrontation that settles a dispute.

clue.text: One may be on course for negotiation

definitions.text: One may be on course for negotiation

parts.words: One may be on course for negotiation
parts.note: reads like a diplomat heading for talks, but means a hurdle or fence on a racecourse or assault course, there to be negotiated, i.e. got over

explanation.surface: Someone is apparently on track to sit down and bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiation' in the sense of getting past or over something, as a horse negotiates a fence on a steeplechase course.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdle or barrier placed on a course is something a competitor must get past.

clue.text: Commit oneself irrevocably, destroying 18 packets?

definitions.meaning: to take a step from which there is no going back
18 down means own, and packets are packet boats, so this is torching one's own vessels

explanation.walkthrough: 18 is the answer to 18 down; packets are mail ships, not parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from armies burning their ships so retreat was impossible, a total commitment.

clue.text: Delicacy singer sank teeth into

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird, so a singer
bit is the past tense of bite

explanation.surface: A songstress bit into a fine morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' is a bird, not a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty piece of food, a dainty morsel.

clue.text: Curious late Incan vocal style

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A singing manner peculiar to an Inca of the late period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' rearranges LATE INCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilena is a smooth flowing lyrical vocal melody or style of singing.

clue.text: Honour former subaltern capturing head of army

indicators.note: capturing means the two pieces close around the extra letter

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a lieutenant, abbreviated Lt, is a subaltern, a junior officer

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Pay tribute to a retired junior officer who seized the army chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' takes the head of army inside the other two pieces; a subaltern is any officer below captain.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to raise them in rank or praise them highly, to honour them.

clue.text: Music pipers improvised originally by prehistoric tower

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: a broch is a round drystone Iron Age tower found in Scotland

explanation.surface: Bagpipers play an impromptu tune beside an ancient stone tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces side by side. A BROCH is a prehistoric round tower peculiar to Scotland, fitting the bagpipe picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is a form of classical bagpipe music, a set of variations on a theme.

clue.text: Lack engagement, being out of gear?

definitions.meaning: to be free, with no appointment in the diary
wearing no clothes, gear being slang for clothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' and 'out of gear' suggest a car's gearbox, but the senses are a free diary and nakedness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to be free of appointments and to be naked.

clue.text: Building in old Arctic plain, right to the fore

indicators.note: to the fore means the named letter is shifted to the very front of the assembled word

parts.note: a tundra is the vast treeless plain of the Arctic

explanation.surface: Somebody has put up a structure out on the frozen northern wastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the fore' moves the R of O + TUNDRA to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, typically one topped with a dome.

clue.text: Dock, perhaps, by head of this river

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: dock is a broad-leaved plant usually treated as a weed, hence the 'perhaps' marking an example

explanation.surface: A quay found at the source of a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a harbour, but it is the plant. 'by' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river forming part of the border between Scotland and England.

clue.text: Stern? One mostly uses the bow

definitions.meaning: Isaac Stern was a celebrated American string virtuoso; the question mark flags him as an example
a fiddler plays chiefly with a bow, though sometimes plucks the strings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' and 'bow' tempt a nautical reading, back and front of a ship, but Stern is the musician and the bow is drawn across strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Stern was a famous player of the four-stringed instrument; any such player mostly bows.

clue.text: Snake shark's left to escape, grabbing fish

indicators.note: grabbing means the fish is held inside the trimmed word
to escape means the named letter gets out of the word for the shark

parts.note: a shark is a swindler, a cheat; the 's stands for has
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A predatory fish lets its catch slip away while seizing another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shark' is a con man, not a fish. 'to escape' drops the L, leaving SWINDER, which 'grabbing' then holds the fish inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidewinder is a desert rattlesnake that moves by looping its body sideways.

clue.text: Like plane taking girl musicians to America, crossing City

indicators.note: crossing means the City abbreviation runs across, inside, the string of pieces

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
EC is the postal district of the City of London
a duo is a pair of musicians
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An aircraft flies a girl and a band across the City to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the tree, not an aircraft. 'crossing' runs the City through the girl, the band and America; 'taking' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane tree sheds its leaves each autumn, so it is a leaf-dropping tree.

clue.text: Boy beginning to suck bull's-eye

parts.note: Len is a man's name, short for Leonard

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A lad starts sucking a round boiled sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A bull's-eye is a striped British boiled sweet, which suits the sucking, but here it means a thick convex glass, as in a bull's-eye lantern.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull's-eye is a small thick convex glass, a kind of magnifying lens, as in old lanterns.

clue.text: City editor initially following female into shelter

indicators.note: into means the pieces go inside the word for shelter

parts.note: a shield gives protection, so a shelter

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss pursues a woman into a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following female' reads as chasing, but gives F + F; 'into' puts E + F + F inside SHIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield is a city in South Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: Own some jumpers on a line

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few sweaters hang on a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is a British word for a sweater; the picture is laundry drying.
explanation.definitionFit: Own and personal both describe what belongs to an individual, as in my own room.

clue.text: Current career

definitions.meaning: a fast current in a channel
to career is to rush along at speed

explanation.definitionFit: A mill race is a strong current of water, and to career madly is to rush or speed.

clue.text: About time male beast replaced companion

indicators.note: about can mean in a disordered state, so it signals the letters are jumbled
replaced means put back in a different place, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: It's high time the male animal was swapped for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' and 'replaced' both signal rearranging T with MALE BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse from the same stable, and by extension a companion or colleague.

clue.text: Performance of cricket side after start of play

indicators.note: after places the cricket side behind the opening part of a play

parts.note: Act I is the opening act of a play
on is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team's showing once the game gets under way.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the ON side is the half of the field to the batter's legs. 'start of play' is ACT I, not P.
explanation.definitionFit: Action can mean a performance or deed, the doing of something.

clue.text: Peninsula where trendy mate holds party

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a do is a party or social event
china means mate, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate = mate

explanation.surface: A fashionable friend throws a party somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Mate is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate). 'holds' puts the party inside the mate, after the trendy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Indochina is the Southeast Asian peninsula containing Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia and neighbours.

clue.text: Doorkeeper blows top about daughter being couch potato

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word wraps around the letter
blows top means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a tiler, or tyler, is the doorkeeper of a Masonic lodge

explanation.surface: A porter loses his temper over a daughter who lounges about.
explanation.walkthrough: A TILER guards a Freemasons' lodge door. 'blows top' leaves ILER; 'about' wraps it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch potato is a lazy person, an idler who lounges about.

clue.text: Rod teachers possibly used

definitions.meaning: a stick or pole, such as a walking ... or a ... of office
a school's teachers are its personnel, hence possibly

explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is a link; the surface hints at a cane once used by teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a rod or stick; it is also the body of employees, e.g. teaching personnel.

clue.text: Concerning a new medical specialism

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine

explanation.surface: About a fresh branch of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the ear, nose and throat specialism.
explanation.definitionFit: Anent is an old or Scots preposition meaning about or regarding.

clue.text: Ruddy bishop leaves, threatening …

indicators.note: leaves means the abbreviation for the cleric departs from the word

parts.note: ruddy and blooming are both mild British euphemisms for bloody
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A blasted clergyman departs, menacingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' is a mild British swear-word, like 'blooming'. The ellipsis links this clue to the next in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Something looming is approaching in a menacing, imminent way, so it is threatening.

clue.text: … earnest male parent outside northern church

indicators.note: outside means the word for male parent wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a sire is a male parent, especially of an animal
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A serious father stands outside a church in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the male parent round the northern and church abbreviations; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere and earnest are synonyms, both meaning genuine and serious in intent.

clue.text: Rich relation given note in payment

indicators.note: in places the relation and note inside the word for payment

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property
a son is a family relation
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: A wealthy relative is handed a banknote as payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests money but is the musical note A; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich voice or sound is deep and full, which is what resonant means.

clue.text: Torn to pieces as roofs may be?

definitions.meaning: severely criticised, as by a reviewer
covered with thin grey roofing tiles of stone

explanation.definitionFit: Slated means harshly criticised, and also describes a roof covered with slates.
